newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr hits 2-yr low on Bank of Canada comment.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr hits 2-yr low on Bank of Canada comment.

text.p: * Canada's dollar hit a two-year low on Thursday at C$1.3945 (US$0.7171) from this morning's open of C$1.3915 (US$0.7186) after comments from a Bank of Canada official led to a selloff and intervention by the Bank of Canada. * The Bank of Canada bought Canadian dollars at the new low to recover the unit to around C$1.3943 (US$0.7172) at the close.
"The market (Canadian dollar) was around C$1.3917 when he made the comments and it's been up to C$1.3945 since," said one trader at a major Canadian bank.
Although the currency recovered to C$1.3934 (US$0.7176) after the Bank of Canada's intervention, renewed selling and weakness emerged on comments by another deputy governor.

Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Chuck Freedman said at a speech in New York that although Fed policy was important to Canada it should not preclude a focus on Canada's domestic economy. Canada's dollar has hit successive two-year lows since the Fed hiked U.S. rates on March 25.
Freedman was asked if the Bank of Canada should follow the Federal Reserve's move to boost rates two weeks ago.

"Obviously Federal Reserve policy is important for Canada," Freedman said at a conference at the Jerome Levy Economics Institute. "That does not preclude a monetary policy that is focused on domestic factors."

Traders said the currency is likely to weaken further overnight as Asian and European investors take stock of their Canadian dollar holdings ahead of economic data out of the U.S. on Friday. A Reuter survey of economists forecast that March producer prices in the U.S. will be reported unchanged.

Economists said investors are sensitive to any economic data which may imply continued inflationary pressures in the U.S. economy and lead the Federal Reserve to raise rates again at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in May.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar dropped to 1.2330 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.2418 marks and dipped to 90.14 yen from Wednesday's 91.18 yen.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
